draft.title: High-risk strategies against resistance
card: Resistance is when staff push back against a change. Managers may respond with high-risk strategies, which can bring quick compliance but carry serious costs.
managers twist or hide information, or shape the story, to steer staff into accepting the change. Staff are not told the full truth.
managers warn of punishment if staff do not go along, such as job loss, fewer hours or a transfer.
These strategies may force change through fast. They can damage trust and morale, and the business's reputation, and staff may leave or resist more.
draft.remember: High-risk strategies may get fast change, but can cost trust, morale and reputation.

a.q: A manager tells staff that a new roster will be introduced, and that anyone who objects may lose shifts. Which strategy is this?
a.why: The manager is warning of punishment if staff object, which is a threat. Manipulation is the tempting wrong answer, but it involves twisting or hiding information, and nothing was hidden here.
a.clue: Look for a warning of punishment.

b.q: Harbour Print plans to move staff to a new site. The owner hides that jobs will be cut and says the move is only about space. Staff comply, then find out. What is the most likely result?
opts: Lost trust and lower morale among staff
Staff gain confidence in the owner's honesty
Staff become more willing to accept future change
The business's reputation as an employer improves
b.why: Hiding the job cuts is manipulation. It may get quick compliance, but when staff find out it can damage trust and morale. Quick compliance does not mean the strategy worked well.
b.clue: Think about how staff feel once they learn the truth.

b.best: Lost trust and lower morale among staff

check.summary: No problems found. The card matches the VCE high-risk strategies of manipulation and threat, and both questions have one clear right answer.
